newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish government bonds blazed a trail higher on Monday, pushed up by a strong dollar and other buoyant foreign debt markets.
Dealers are awaiting December CPI data, due on Wednesday, and then Thursday's regular repo auction, hoping to see the first cut of the year in the 6.25-percent official rate.
"I do not really believe in the end they'll cut so soon. But in the market, there are clear hopes," a dealer in Madrid said.
Short-end yields rose in anticipation of an easing, with one-year deposits trading at 5.50 percent. The Bank of Spain most recently cut 50 basis points off the rate on December 13.
According to a Reuter poll of economists, December CPI is seen up 3.2 percent year-on-year, unchanged from November.
But some dealers said the peseta's strength, which ended on Monday at 83.46/3.48 versus the mark, could prod the central bank to act soon, dealer said.
On the cash debt market, the 10-year spread over Bunds hit a record low at 91 bps before widening back to 93 bps, its previous low from last Friday.
The spread to US T-bonds also narrowed a bp.
